_comment: Full of round holes, cut through whatever it is said of. The rock chosen porous: isolated voids you break
into rather than tunnels you walk along, wet near the surface and dry far below (`Carvers.POROUS`); `dry porous
rock` keeps them dry. `porous features` holes the rock the features build above the ground, and a named one
(`porous trees`, `porous obelisks`) everything it lays; `porous structures` and `porous villages` are holed through
their walls and floors, never through what holds something. `porous surface` is the ground pocked with pits,
like pumice; `porous landmass` the land itself holed through above the ground, in great round holes; and
`porous underground` the caves a sponge of big round pocks, now and then joined by a crawl; and `porous sea` the
water holding bubbles of air suspended in it, as Riven's does, that flood if the water beside one is disturbed.
